title: How Did My Heart Rejoice to Hear
description: How Did My Heart Rejoice to Hear in Tonic Solfa to ST ANNE, doh is C: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 6 verses and a piano.
about: Isaac Watts wrote these words for The Psalms of David Imitated in the Language of the New Testament (1719): Psalm 122, part 1, headed “Going to church”.
Watts' psalms were printed without tunes and sung to any tune of their metre, Common Metre (8.6.8.6). This page sets the words to ST ANNE; any other Common Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: How did my heart re-joice to hear My friends de-vout-ly say, "In Zi-on let us all ap-pear, "And keep the sol-emn day!"

lines: How did my heart rejoice to hear
I love her gates, I love the road:
Stands like a palace built for God,
Up to her courts with joys unknown
The Son of David holds his throne,
He hears our praises and complaints;
Divides the sinners from the saints,
Peace be within this sacred place,
With holy gifts, and heavenly grace
My soul shall pray for Zion still,
There my best friends, my kindred dwell,

source: Isaac Watts, The Psalms of David Imitated (1719)
licence: Public domain: Isaac Watts died in 1748.
credits: Words by Isaac Watts (1674–1748), public domain; set to ST ANNE by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
